headline: Rice University researchers plan to use a NASA AI weather model to create thousands of computer-made hurricanes so insurers and planners can judge storm risk better.
score_reason: A university's announcement of a project plan with no results yet.
importance_line: Homeowners and communities in hurricane-prone areas, and the insurers who cover them, could get clearer risk estimates, but this is a university's own plan with no tested results, and it is not yet shown that the artificial storms will be realistic enough.
summary: Rice University says two of its researchers are building an open-source tool on NASA's Prithvi-WxC AI weather model to create about 10,000 computer-made hurricanes, because real major storms are too rare to show how often and how badly they could hit. They hope the simulated storms will give insurers and other researchers better estimates of wind, rain and property risk, though the release reports no results yet.
